newsitem.title: USA: Nevada Energy board sued by former directors.
newsitem.headline: Nevada Energy board sued by former directors.

text.p: Two former directors of Nevada Energy Co have sued the company's new president and board, alleging that they misappropriated assets after taking control of Nevada in May.

In a complaint filed Thursday in the Delaware Chancery Court and made available to Reuters Monday, plaintiffs Michael Kassouff and Richard Cascarilla, also a former officer, claim the alleged misappropriation began when the Irish corporation Waterford Trust took control of Nevada in return for $5 million in equity financing.

Nevada directors Peter Cannell, Charles Cain and John Goold, who are also on the Waterford board, allegedly diverted "approximately $1.2 million in Nevada Energy's Funds for non- corporate purposes;" usurped for themselves a business opportunity intended for Nevada; and, together with Nevada president Stefan Tevis, breached their duty of loyalty to Nevada by ignoring "illegal sales" of common stock and allowing the conversion of "preferred stock into common stock at an artificially depressed price."
The business offer was a proposal in May that Nevada buy Telecom Technologies Inc.

According to court papers, the offer was allegedly diverted by the director defendants to a subsidiary of the Isle of Man company Wina Associates which then allegedly resold Telecom to Nevada, "thus giving Telecom and indirectly Messrs (Pattison) Hayton, Goold, Cannell and Cain a profit of over $2 million in a very short period of time at Nevada Energy's expense."

Kassouff, who owns 200,000 shares of Nevada common stock, and Cascarilla, a former officer who owns 10,000 shares, allege that the Waterford directors who replaced the incumbent Nevada board acted "at the direction of Pattison Hayton," an Australian citizen living in Palm Springs, California.

According to court papers, Hayton "makes all of Nevada Energy's material business decisions and dominates or controls...(the defendants) through his control of Waterford and Golden Chance," an Isle of Man private company.

The plaintiffs claim that in September, Cascarilla and former Nevada president Jeffrey Antisdel were ousted when they tried to notify the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission through an electronic Form 8-K filing that Golden Chance was in "default on its obligations" to provide equity financing to Nevada through an agreement with Waterford.
The plaintiffs seeks unspecified damages against the defendants on behalf of Nevada Energy, a nominal defendant.
Calls to Nevada Energy's offices in Santa Barbara, Calif., could not be completed because the telephone has been disconnected, an operator told Reuters.
